changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 4 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/5926-empty-action-visible-when.md`

- names `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `visibleWhen` is not a per-block concern in this platform. It is enforced **once, generically**, in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`: `shouldHide` tests `visibleWhen` ahead of the hoisted `visible` (objectui#5454), sets `_hidden`, and the `_hidden` early return fires **before** the registry dispatches. A block renderer cannot ignore the gate, because it never sees the node.

### `.changeset/7319-dead-schemarenderer-retired.md`

- names `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > `packages/components/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` was a 28-line component carrying the same export name as the real renderer in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx`. Nothing reached it: it is absent from the package barrel, no file in the repo imports it by any form, and the package's `exports` map has no subpath that resolves to it.

### `.changeset/7415-action-type-input-rename.md`

- names `SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > **Census of the authored corpus, measured before the rename, not assumed.** Across 4,797 files in `examples/`, `apps/console/`, `content/docs/` and `packages/`: **zero** authored nodes set the input. 517 JSON files (433 of them the schema catalog) contain 2,410 `type`-bearing nodes and **no** `action:button` / `action:icon` node at all — control: 127 plain `button` nodes on the same walk. 207 parsed fenced JSON blocks in md/mdx carry **5** `action:button` nodes, all of them `{ type, label, icon?, action }` — the discriminator plus the `action` channel, none setting an execution type — control: 28 plain `button` nodes, and the count independently matches the corpus census already recorded in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` ("`action:button` (5 nodes)"). No docs page documents the input; no catalog entry uses the components. So the rename breaks no authored document in this repo.

### `.changeset/9959-refused-data-prop-warn-reset.md`

- names `SchemaRenderer.tsx` → `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` — edited by this change

  > The dedupe `Set` behind the objectui#9571 / objectui#9758 diagnostic — "the authored `data` key was NOT passed to the component as a React prop" — lived in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` with nothing able to clear it, while every other dev diagnostic in this package's `utils/` directory pairs its `Set` with an exported test-only reset. `propsBagDiagnostic.ts` states the consequence in its own reset's docblock: the second test to assert the same warning reads the first test's dedupe entry and sees silence, "a green run that checked nothing". The absence direction is the dangerous one — a test asserting this warning did NOT fire for a `type#id` an earlier test already warned for is green whatever the renderer does, and it reports that green as coverage.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `29b45f6a0` (merge-base with origin/main): 8 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1588 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2176 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36326854007)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e8b96c0161780a3bbf6f0d4f3cbfd51f90de6400`

### ① Derived judgments

Everything below comes from reading the code. No probe was run: nothing needed execution to settle.

- **One evaluator, not two: holds.**
  - `configEvaluationScope`, `evaluateConfigValueWith` and `evaluateConfigBagWith` are line-for-line the base memo's code:
    - the scope has the same spread order: predicateScope, then `current_user` from `predicateScope?.user`, then `record` only when the row is a non-array object, then `page`;
    - the per-key rule is the same ternary: `params` bag, data object, `preservePredicateEnvelope`;
    - the loop is the same `{ ...bag }` plus per-entry overwrite.
  - The memo now calls all three: `new ExpressionEvaluator(configEvaluationScope(...))`, `evaluateConfigValue` delegates to `evaluateConfigValueWith`, and `newSchema.properties = evaluateConfigBagWith(evaluator, rawPropertiesBag)`. The node-level `params` leg and `rawPropertiesBag` (used by the objectui#5756 diagnostic) are unchanged.
  - Ordinary `SchemaRenderer` nodes see no behaviour change.
  - `evaluateConfigBagInScope` builds a fresh evaluator from those same pieces. `SchemaRenderer` itself never calls it (this falsifies a changeset sentence; see ②).
- **Double evaluation: none on any path.**
  - Bar inline members: `action:button`, `action:icon`, and group-placed members routed to `action:button`. The bar evaluates them once in `renderMember`. Neither `action-button.tsx` nor `action-icon.tsx` evaluates again; they only read `readStaticParamValues`. No `SchemaRenderer` sits between them.
  - Bar overflow (menu-placed, spilled, and `systemActions`): `combinedOverflow` is passed raw, and `action:menu` evaluates it once, at run time.
  - `action:group` inline and dropdown, and `action:menu`: evaluated once, in `handleExecute`.
  - A bar node's own `actions` array is not walked by the memo, which is shallow, and no host found pre-evaluates members.
  - The "evaluated once" claim is true but not pinned. No test uses a row value that itself contains `${…}`.
- **Scope parity: holds.**
  - The hook reads exactly `usePredicateScope()`, `useRecordContext()?.data` and `usePageVariables().variables`, the same three the memo reads.
  - `SchemaRenderer` renders no provider between itself and its renderer, so a container reads the same contexts a member's own `SchemaRenderer` would.
  - `current_user` is bound the same way, the CEL envelope is kept, and a data object passes through, all through the shared rule.
- **Ruling A: code holds; one text gap.**
  - A node-level object `params` is still ignored with exactly one warning on every path:
    - bar inline, through `readStaticParamValues`;
    - group, menu and bar overflow, through `readActionEntryParamValues`, still called on the non-array branch.
  - The pins check this on all 8 paths.
  - New silent case: a `type: 'api'` group/menu item that carries both a node-level object and `properties.params`. `properties.params` now wins, and the objectstack#5777 payload is dropped with no warning. The PR body says the api window is "unchanged" in the same bullet where it says `properties.params` wins over it; that is self-contradictory (wording fix in ②).
  - **Docblock rewrite:** the new sentence is true in behaviour at head.
    - Group/menu items read `properties.params`.
    - `element:button` reads only `readActionEntryParamValues`; `elements.tsx:248` confirms it.
    - `page:header` never reads `properties.params`: `containers.tsx:1851` dispatches the action itself and never mounts `action:menu`.
  - **It is not consistent with Zone 1**, the file-top docblock. Zone 1 justifies `properties.params` as "the node's **already-declared** config bag", but `UIActionSchema` (`packages/types/src/ui-action.ts:568`) declares no `properties` and has no index signature. That is why commit `570de551d2` had to loosen `withEvaluatedProperties` to `T extends object` (TS2559).
  - So on a container member the channel is read off the authored JSON, not off a declared key. A TS author of `ActionGroupSchema.actions` gets a type error (TS2353) writing it without a cast.
  - The PM claim's own `Clause-②: no` rationale ("already-declared `properties.params`") is false for members.
  - Ruling A ("no new value-bag key is declared") rules out declaring it here, so this is a wording duty, not a code blocker.
  - Replacement parenthetical in `static-params.ts`: "(An `action:group` / `action:menu` item is also a container member, so its static values are read from `properties.params` and evaluated by the container through {@link readMemberStaticParamValues} (objectui#10290). `UIActionSchema` declares no `properties`, so on a container member this bag is read off the authored object, not off a declared key. `element:button`'s inline `action` and `page:header`'s actions do not read `properties.params`.)"
  - Also recommended: Zone 1's "`SchemaRenderer` template-evaluates every string leaf of that bag" should add "; a container member, which never passes through `SchemaRenderer`, is evaluated by its container with the same rule and scope (`useConfigBagEvaluator`, objectui#10290)".
- **React rules: clean.**
  - `useConfigBagEvaluator()` is called unconditionally, before every early return, in all three containers.
  - Inside the hook, three hooks are called unconditionally.
  - `handleExecute` deps `[execute, evaluateBag]` are correct.
  - The hook returns a fresh function each render, so `handleExecute` and the `ActionAutoTrigger` `run` also churn every render. `useAutoTriggerOnce` is guarded by refs, so correctness does not rest on identity (AGENTS.md #10). The cost is small.
  - The hook lives in `hooks/` to keep `SchemaRenderer.tsx` out of the compiler purity lint (the dev's measured reason). The hooks/index-to-SchemaRenderer import cycle is safe: the binding is hoisted and used only at call time.
- **Pins: sound, with gaps.**
  - All 8 container paths are covered, and the control (a top-level `action:button` through `SchemaRenderer`, green on base) is real.
  - The 8 "resolved" rows assert `recordId: 'rec_1'` and are not tautological. The quoted ablation reddening exactly those 8 fits the source.
  - The 8 node-level rows are regression guards that are green on base, not fix pins.
  - Not pinned:
    - evaluation happens once;
    - group/menu with an array `params` forward `params: staticValues` too (a new key on that branch; `toEqual` ignores `undefined`);
    - `properties.params` wins over the api window.
  - These are non-blocking; recommend adding the first.

### ② Semver level

- **The exports reach the entry.**
  - `packages/react/src/index.ts:9` has `export * from './SchemaRenderer.js'`, which carries `evaluateConfigBagInScope`.
  - `:11` has `export * from './hooks/index.js'`, and `hooks/index.ts:48` has `export * from './useConfigBagEvaluator.js'`.
  - `package.json` `exports` is `"."` only, so both are public API.
- **`'@object-ui/react': patch` is wrong. `Clause-②` is yes (widening).**
  - Two new public exports widen the published surface. Per AGENTS.md, `yes` takes at least `minor`.
  - The repo precedent says the same: `.changeset/10288-config-bag-data-object-source.md` and `7867-action-params-templates.md` are both `'@object-ui/react': minor` with a "Declared as a minor (Clause-②)" sentence.
  - CI cannot catch this. "Changeset Bump Policy" only refuses `major`.
  - Because of the fixed group, the whole group releases at this minor.
- **Keeping it internal is not feasible.**
  - `@object-ui/components` can import only through the `"."` entry, so `useConfigBagEvaluator` must be public.
  - Route (b) would avoid new exports, but dropdown items are `DropdownMenuItem` leaves, so (b) is not viable there.
  - `evaluateConfigBagInScope` has no consumer outside the hook. It could be kept off the entry by moving it and its helpers into a module `index.ts` does not re-export. That narrowing is optional; one export remains either way, so `minor` stands.
- **The changeset, sentence by sentence.** The first paragraph is accurate. Four sentences are wrong or overstated:
  - "reach the handler **exactly** as a top-level `action:button`'s do": overstated. The unevaluated-expression diagnostic does not run for container members (the dev's own out-of-scope note).
  - "A node-level `params` object is still not read as values": imprecise. Group/menu items of `type: 'api'` still forward it (objectstack#5777 window).
  - "It returns the `SchemaRenderer` memo's own `properties` evaluation": loose. It returns a function.
  - "exported beside `SchemaRenderer`, **which applies the same rule through it**": false. `SchemaRenderer` never calls `evaluateConfigBagInScope`.
- **Replacement changeset** (the frontmatter plus paragraphs 2 to 4; paragraph 1 is kept):
  ```
  ---
  '@object-ui/components': patch
  '@object-ui/react': minor
  ---
  ```
  - Paragraph 2: "Each container now evaluates its members' `properties` with the evaluator and scope `SchemaRenderer` uses: `action:bar` where it composes an inline member, and `action:group` / `action:menu` when they run an item. A container member's static values therefore reach the handler as a top-level `action:button`'s do, with one difference: the development-build unevaluated-expression diagnostic runs in the `SchemaRenderer` memo, so it does not report an unresolvable template on a container member. An item that carries an `ActionParam[]` input list forwards both, as `action:button` does. A node-level `params` object is still not read as values (objectui#10289). The one exception is unchanged from objectui#10462: an `action:group` / `action:menu` item of `type: 'api'` still forwards it as the request payload (objectstack#5777 window), unless the item also carries a `properties.params` bag, which now takes precedence."
  - Paragraph 3: "`@object-ui/react` exports `useConfigBagEvaluator()` for this. It returns a function that applies the `SchemaRenderer` memo's `properties` evaluation (the same per-key rule and the same `record` / `current_user` / `page` scope) to a config bag rendered without `SchemaRenderer`.
